title: Capacity Command Deck: unified ops canvas for dedicated inference clusters
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a single-pane 'Capacity Command Deck' for Dedicated clusters that surfaces actionable health signals, cost/leak indicators, and fast controls for autoscaling and burst policies. The canvas should enable on-call engineers and SREs to triage anomalies quickly, run temporary burst adjustments, and initiate rollouts or fallbacks with minimal context switching.
background: Current console screens are fragmented across 'Pool Details', 'Health', and 'Scaling' tabs. Support teams report frequent OOM/latency incidents where the root cause is spread across different views. This card consolidates signals into a prioritised ops canvas and explores micro-interactions for quick remediation.
acceptance_criteria: Single view shows top-5 clusters by risk (combined score of error rate, latency outliers, headroom, and queue depth)
Operations can apply a burst override to a cluster (duration + % of capacity) from the canvas and see immediate simulated cost delta
Rollout shortcut executes a canary rollback policy and links to the model variant in the catalog
All widgets have keyboard focus states and pass basic a11y color-contrast checks
Design spec includes token-level cost display and a compact mode for 1366x768 screens
decisions: Surface a composite 'Risk Score' rather than individual ranked signals to reduce noise for first-pass triage
Use a vertical 'card stack' layout on narrow screens and a 3-column grid on wide screens for highest information density
Expose burst as a lightweight 'playground' modal that previews cost and latency impact before commit
Defer deep query/filter tools (logs/trace drilldowns) to dedicated links to reduce scope for this iteration
tradeoffs_considered: High density vs cognitive load: prioritized showing signal + action; removed low-utility metrics to avoid distraction
Interactivity vs security: inline scaling actions require scoped RBAC checks; design includes micro-confirmations to satisfy audits
Simulated cost preview vs real-time accuracy: prototype uses cached rate estimates to avoid spamming billing backend
review_feedback: PM (Liam): prefer a one-click 'snooze alerts' for noise bursts; suggested adding a heatmap legend
SRE (Sofia): require a fast-path to evict non-critical workloads before burst increases; suggested 'evict list' integration
Eng (Karthik): requested API contract for simulated cost estimates and advised to limit preview calls to once per 30s
usability_notes: User tests (n=7) showed median time-to-triage reduced from 7m -> 3.2m with the composite risk card
Participants favored inline previews for burst cost over navigating to billing pages
Confusion arose around 'headroom' label; renamed to 'available throughput' in updated copy
next_steps: Finalize iconography and microcopy for risk legend (due 2025-02-20)
Hand off annotated tokens and responsive specs to frontend team (ENG-4129)
Add RBAC guard flows and micro-confirmation UX to security review (target 2025-02-24)
Run an accessibility audit on the 3-column layout before design freeze
